scope: Offline semantic review of all seven actual factorykit.runtime.standing_instructions custom-section outputs. Not launch readiness, live execution or product acceptance.
reviewer_independence_disclosure: This subagent authored the four PR2 additions. checks.evidence: Each seat mandate and all three shared protocols were read compositionally, including the identical shared mandate contract, launcher boundary and rendered roster/budgets. New paragraphs describe requirement relationships, independent oracles, counterexamples, valid controls, side effects and coverage without product entities or seeded tests. Keyword/credential scans are supplementary only.

Planning review explicitly is not product acceptance. Owner and QA evidence cannot replace the separate Reviewer decision; exact committed candidates, clean separate review checkout, required isolation, and full handoffs remain required. Reviewer cannot repair and approve the same candidate. Coordinator cannot waive required behavior or a failed gate.

Every actual render injects max_repairs=3, max_active_seats=1 and approved=false from the same configuration. Shared protocols prioritize task-configured limits, require changed diagnosis after repeated failures, forbid exceeding finite limits, and require bounded outcomes. New paragraphs do not add attempts or reset budgets.

Roster metadata describes configured seats. Standing text says connected smoke execution remains unverified until checked, membership is insufficient proof of responsiveness, admission does not establish collaboration or acceptance, and nominal ownership must not simulate contribution. No new live rehearsal or material-contribution claim is made.

Designer retains rendered review tied to revision/viewports/browser evidence; Frontend distinguishes mocked, real-browser and connected-service proof. Missing tools, skipped/empty suites and generated configuration cannot prove integration.

limits_and_notes: The unchanged mandate fallback mentions at most two repairs, while the shared protocol prioritizes task-configured limits and the rendered numeric ceiling is three. This audit confirms no permission to exceed three; it does not prove agents will consume all three attempts or resolve every interpretation identically.
